claims.claim: Generative adversarial networks were developed by Ian Goodfellow and colleagues in June 2014.
claims.episode_span: The paper, “Generative Adversarial Nets,” was submitted in June 2014
claims.supporting_quote: The concept was initially developed by Ian Goodfellow and his colleagues in June 2014.

claims.claim: Goodfellow did his PhD at the Université de Montréal under the supervision of Yoshua Bengio (with Aaron Courville), completing it in February 2015 — i.e., he was a PhD student there when GANs were proposed.
claims.episode_span: Ian Goodfellow was a PhD student at the University of Montreal working under Yoshua Bengio when he proposed Generative Adversarial Networks
claims.supporting_quote: his PhD in machine learning from the Université de Montréal in February 2015, under the supervision of Yoshua Bengio and Aaron Courville

claims.claim: The paper 'Generative Adversarial Nets' was presented at the Neural Information Processing Systems conference (NIPS 2014).
claims.episode_span: and presented at the Neural Information Processing Systems conference that December
claims.supporting_quote: Goodfellow, Ian; Pouget-Abadie, Jean; Mirza, Mehdi; Xu, Bing; Warde-Farley, David; Ozair, Sherjil; Courville, Aaron; Bengio, Yoshua (2014). Generative Adversarial Nets (PDF) . Proceedings of the International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2014).

claims.claim: The term 'deepfake' originated in late 2017 from a Reddit user named 'deepfakes' who shared face-swapped videos.
claims.episode_span: The first public demonstration of face-swapping video arrived in late 2017 on Reddit, where a user released code
claims.supporting_quote: The term deepfake originated in late 2017 from a Reddit user named "deepfakes".

claims.claim: Reddit banned the r/deepfakes subreddit on 7 February 2018 for violating its involuntary-pornography policy.
claims.episode_span: Reddit banned deepfake pornography in February 2018; Twitter and Pornhub followed with similar prohibitions
claims.supporting_quote: Reddit banned the r/deepfakes subreddit on 7 February 2018, due to the policy violation of "involuntary pornography".

claims.claim: In April 2018 Jordan Peele and BuzzFeed released a deepfake of Barack Obama (with Peele's voice, depicting Obama cursing and insulting Donald Trump) as a public service announcement about deepfakes.
claims.episode_span: in April 2018 a video of Barack Obama appeared to call Donald Trump a “complete dipshit,” created by comedian Jordan Peele and BuzzFeed to illustrate the risk
claims.supporting_quote: In April 2018, Jordan Peele collaborated with BuzzFeed to create a deepfake of Barack Obama with Peele's voice; it served as a public service announcement to increase awareness of deepfakes.

claims.claim: An October 2019 report by cybersecurity firm Deeptrace estimated that 96% of deepfake videos online were pornographic.
claims.episode_span: By 2019, estimates from Deeptrace Labs suggested more than 96 percent of online deepfake videos were non-consensual pornography
claims.supporting_quote: A report published in October 2019 by Dutch cybersecurity startup Deeptrace estimated that 96% of all deepfakes online were pornographic.
